tools.name: edit_diagram
tools.description:
Edit a specific page in the current diagram by ID-based operations (update/add/delete cells).

All-or-nothing: if any operation fails, nothing is applied and every failure is listed.

Freshness: the server remembers the last diagram state you have seen, and rejects this call only if the user edited the diagram in the browser since then. You do NOT need to call get_diagram before every edit: a rejected call changes nothing and includes the current XML of the page, so you can rebuild your operations and retry.

Call get_diagram first only when you don't know the current diagram content (cell IDs, structure) — e.g. the diagram wasn't created in this conversation, or you're unsure your memory of it is accurate.

Multi-page targeting:
- page_id / page_name / page_index are optional; when all omitted, the FIRST page is targeted
- Use list_pages to discover what pages exist

Operations:
- add: Add a new cell. Provide cell_id (new unique id within the page) and new_xml. One cell per operation.
- update: Replace an existing cell by its id. Provide cell_id and complete new_xml.
- delete: Remove a cell by its id. Only cell_id is needed. Its children and connected edges are deleted too, so give only a container's id.

For add/update, new_xml is the complete mxCell (inside its <object> wrapper when it has custom data, see the drawing guide) in the compact form (a shape with x, y, w, h; an edge with source and target). No XML comments. Every " inside new_xml must be escaped as \" in the JSON.

Example - Add a rectangle on the default (first) page:
{"operations": [{"operation": "add", "cell_id": "rect-1", "new_xml": "<mxCell id=\"rect-1\" value=\"Hello\" style=\"rounded=1;\" x=\"100\" y=\"100\" w=\"120\" h=\"60\"/>"}]}

Example - Delete a cell on the default page:
{"operations": [{"operation": "delete", "cell_id": "rect-1"}]}

tools.name: export_diagram
tools.description:
Export the current diagram to a file. Supports .drawio (XML), .png, .svg, and .drawio.svg (an SVG with the diagram embedded, which draw.io and load_diagram can open again). The format is auto-detected from the file extension, or can be specified explicitly. Images get a 20 px margin; a PNG has a white background (or the page's own background color) unless transparent is true.

Multi-page behaviour:
- .drawio with NO page selector: writes the full <mxfile> (all pages).
- .drawio with a page selector: writes a single-page <mxfile> containing only that page.
- .png / .svg with NO page selector: exports the currently active page in the browser.
- .png with a page selector: renders that page without changing what the user sees.
- .svg / .drawio.svg with a page selector: temporarily loads that page into the browser, captures it, then restores the full document (the user sees a brief flicker).

format.description: Export format. If omitted, detected from file extension. Defaults to drawio.

transparent.description: PNG only: a transparent background instead of white. Default false.

tools.name: export_diagram
tools.description:
Export the current diagram to a file. Supports .drawio (XML), .png, .svg, and .drawio.svg (an SVG with the diagram embedded, which draw.io and load_diagram can open again). The format is auto-detected from the file extension, or can be specified explicitly. Images get a 20 px margin; a PNG has a white background (or the page's own background color) unless transparent is true.

Multi-page behaviour:
- .drawio with NO page selector: writes the full <mxfile> (all pages).
- .drawio with a page selector: writes a single-page <mxfile> containing only that page.
- .png / .svg with NO page selector: exports the currently active page in the browser.
- .png with a page selector: renders that page without changing what the user sees.
- .svg / .drawio.svg with a page selector: temporarily loads that page into the browser, captures it, then restores the full document (the user sees a brief flicker).

path.description: Absolute file path to save to (e.g. <local>/diagram.png). Relative paths resolve against the MCP server's working directory, which is often not your project.

format.description: Export format. If omitted, detected from file extension. Defaults to drawio.

transparent.description: PNG only: a transparent background instead of white. Default false.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
